name: Primes on Interval
description: You've decided to carry out a survey in the theory of prime numbers. Let us remind you that a prime number is a positive integer that has exactly two distinct positive integer divisors. Consider positive integers a , a + 1 , ... , b ( a ≤ b ) . You want to find the minimum integer l (1 ≤ l ≤ b - a + 1) such that for any integer x ( a ≤ x ≤ b - l + 1) among l integers x , x + 1 , ... , x + l - 1 there are at least k prime numbers. Find and print the required minimum l . If no value l meets the described limitations, print -1.
input_specification: A single line contains three space-separated integers a , b , k ( 1 ≤ a , b , k ≤ 10 6 ; a ≤ b ).
output_specification: In a single line print a single integer — the required minimum l . If there's no solution, print -1.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
